subject: Would a simple GUI like this be of use (or is there already something like this) ? TY

messages.author: 326e43105ab92d1e
messages.subject: Would a simple GUI like this be of use (or is there already something like this) ? TY
parts:
Hello,

I made a little GUI that maybe can be adapted for lavaan.

In reality, I was in the process of making a full SEM software, in order to learn from within how all the calculations are made in Amos (which is the program I am most used to).

But I ended up interrupting my work after being able to compute OLS Multiple Regressions via Apache Commons Math Lib, and Covariances/Correlations.

I still intend to continue the work I was doing, and will try to do all computations with my own code, but in the meanwhile, I have what I think is a nice GUI, that is only missing to allow latent variables to be draw.

For the diagram in the image, the GUI now is producing a syntax such as:

varA->varD
varB->varD
varC->varD
varC->varE
varD->varE
varA<->varB
varA<->varC
varB<->varC

I only have to replace the syntax.

Of all the things that are missing, undo is the one that may give me more work. But it can be fun implementing. It already supports drag and drop, and it saves and opens the daigrams and connects to the desired database, exposing the variables in that database for selection.

My question is this: is there any other GUI that allows SEM diagrams to be drawn as easily as in AMOS?

If not, what do you think of this (working, although buggy) mockup ?

Thank you. Best regards,

Luís

Hi.

Onyx provides a free GUI that can be used with lavaan.

http://onyx.brandmaier.de

Other than that, I think that all major commercial SEM software include path diagram editors.

Mikko

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Would a simple GUI like this be of use (or is there already something like this) ? TY
parts:
Luis,
Hats off to your effort to code a SEM GUI, especially if you did it in R.  Here are some thoughts.

You would not need to code the analyses in R because you could have your GUI call lavaan (or another package) in the background.  In a Model-View-Controller architecture, lavaan would be the model component.  Your GUI would only need to provide the view and the controller.

Experience with GUIs in commercial software suggests that GUI specification is useful for small models but usually becomes less convenient than script specifications as models become more complex.

One thing that might make a more unique contribution to the ecosystem than a draw canvass GUI would be a GUI that provides a text editing environment for writing lavaan model syntax that provided real time syntax evaluation.  Many might find it helpful to have a model syntax editor that color coded different elements of lavaan syntax and flagged syntax errors.  Even better if the editor could be installed with an R package and launched in R from the R command window.

Keith
